sources: Takshashila Op-Eds (NDTV, The Hindu, Times of India, Firstpost)

posts.title: All Things Policy | Win-Win Energy Policy
posts.description: Public conversation about energy and climate tends to default to a sense of unavoidable trade-offs, where every gain is assumed to carry an equal and offsetting loss. India's own record complicates that pessimism. Fly ash, once a disposal problem piling up in ash ponds beside thermal plants, now moves into cement, bricks, and roads. Clean cooking gas has reached households that had never had a connection. None of these was costless, and none was free of design flaws, but each shows that well-constructed policy can improve health, the environment, and the economy at the same time. Join Srinivasan Iyengar and Arindam Goswami as this episode of All Things Policy uses the ethanol debate as an entry point to a wider question: how India can keep designing pragmatic energy policy that treats elec

posts.title: Turbulence | Tariffs and Trade Disruption — Trump and Beyond
posts.description: Tariffs are back, industrial policy is fashionable again, and over the past year the United States, the country that helped build and maintain the open trading system, has spent its energy tearing holes in it, taxing allies and rivals alike. The popular verdict in India is grim: a global trade war is on, the rules-based order is finished, and we are caught in the crossfire. But is that really what's happening? In this episode of Turbulence, Anupam Manur is joined by Devashish Mitra — Professor of Economics at Syracuse University's Maxwell School, and the economist who has written extensively on the political economy of trade policy. posts.title: #23 Gerrymandering and the New Rules of US Politics
posts.description: The Supreme Court’s Louisiana v. Callais decision weakens protections against electoral maps that dilute minority voting power, making it harder to challenge districts through intent-based rather than outcome-based standards. The piece analyses how both parties increasingly treat redistricting as a partisan tool, drawing comparisons to India’s independent delimitation system.
posts.author: Brigadier Anil Raman

posts.title: Why The Blockade Is Trump's Best Card
posts.description: Abhishek Kadiyala argues that a naval blockade of Iran is the Trump administration's strategically optimal move — it avoids triggering the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock while maintaining pressure, keeping congressional hawks satisfied and doves outmanoeuvred.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: Analysing US Congressional Oversight on the Iran War
posts.description: This policy brief examines congressional responses to President Trump's military action against Iran, which began February 28, 2026. The analysis explores two institutional mechanisms through which Congress can exercise oversight: the War Powers Resolution (WPR) and budgetary appropriations authority. The brief identifies deep partisan and intra-party divisions, tracks multiple failed legislative attempts, and concludes that budgetary restraint represents Congress's most viable constraint mechanism.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: #22 Why are Hegseth’s purges different?
posts.description: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s removal of 21 senior military officials reflects personal power consolidation rather than ideological realignment. The author argues these actions undermine institutional military independence — and with midterm elections approaching, the gap between the stated rationale and actual logic may prove a political liability.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: #21 — A Generational Mid-term?
posts.description: At least one in eight members of Congress is departing ahead of the 2026 midterms — the highest retirement rate since 1992. The piece examines the three forces driving the exodus: institutional frustration with a gridlocked Congress, deepening partisan polarisation that makes legislating increasingly thankless, and a declining appeal of federal service relative to state-level or private-sector alternatives.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: 35 US Lawmakers Just Moved A Bill That Could Upend Indian Techies' Careers
posts.description: Brigadier Anil Raman examines a bipartisan congressional bill, co-sponsored by 35 House members, that would tighten H-1B visa rules and add domestic hiring requirements — legislation that directly affects Indian technology professionals and reflects the populist electoral pressures shaping Congress ahead of the 2026 midterms.
posts.author: Brigadier Anil Raman

posts.title: The Iran Brief: US Congress and Trump
posts.description: With the 60-day War Powers Resolution clock ticking, this episode examines why Congress has again failed to constrain Trump's military operations against Iran. The panel unpacks the structural weaknesses of the War Powers Resolution — including the Trump administration filing only classified reports. The core argument: the real obstacle is political will, not legal ambiguity.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala, Brigadier Anil Raman & Soren Dayton

posts.title: Three Things May Happen At The End Of The 14-Day Ceasefire (Or Earlier)
posts.description: Kadiyala maps three possible trajectories as the US-brokered Iran ceasefire nears its deadline: a negotiated settlement, a return to hostilities requiring fresh congressional authorisation, or an ambiguous freeze that leaves war powers questions unresolved.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: The Iran Brief: Why Is US Congress Failing To Stop Trump On Iran?
posts.description: Congress has repeatedly failed to constrain President Trump's military actions against Iran despite multiple legislative attempts. The episode traces failed resolutions invoking the War Powers Resolution of 1973 — sponsored by Tim Kaine, Thomas Massie, Ro Khanna, and Chris Murphy — and examines how partisanship, electoral incentives, and ideological splits (cutting across party lines) have shaped outcomes.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala & Bhumika Sevkani

posts.title: #19 The “March-uary” of Iran War Bills
posts.description: How and why has the Congress failed to stop Trump’s war in Iran
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: All Things Policy | The Iran Brief: War and MAGA Fissures
posts.description: Takshashila Institution's All Things Policy examines the fissures within the MAGA coalition in Congress over the Iran strikes, and what the split reveals about Congress’s capacity — and willingness — to constrain the executive on war powers.
posts.author: Lokendra Sharma & Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: If Trump Puts Troops In Iran
posts.description: Kadiyala examines the constitutional and political consequences of deploying US ground forces to Iran, including how the War Powers Resolution would be triggered, what bipartisan opposition in Congress looks like, and why the 60-day clock becomes Trump's most immediate legislative constraint.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: All Things Policy — US Congress, War Powers & Iran
posts.description: An episode of All Things Policy examining the US Congress's role and response in the context of military action, war powers, and the legislative dynamics of the current Congress.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala & Brigadier Anil Raman

posts.title: The system bends, it rarely breaks, says U.S. Congressional expert Matthew Glassman
posts.description: Brigadier Anil Raman interviews Matthew Glassman, a leading expert on US Congressional procedure, who argues that despite Trump-era stress tests, American democratic institutions — particularly Congressional checks on executive power — are resilient by design, though not invulnerable.
posts.author: Brigadier Anil Raman

posts.title: #18 Why and How Has Congress Responded Differently to Venezuela, Greenland, and Iran?
posts.description: Dossier in Brief: comparing the legislative responses to three distinct foreign policy crises and what the divergence reveals about congressional incentives.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: There Are Two Big Problems Trump May Run Into If He Actually Attacks Iran
posts.description: Kadiyala identifies two structural obstacles to Trump striking Iran: the War Powers Resolution's 60-day constraint and the fractured Republican coalition in Congress, where fiscal hawks and libertarian-leaning members resist open-ended military commitments without explicit authorisation.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: How Congress, Pentagon contain POTUS overreach and how India should leverage it
posts.description: Brigadier Anil Raman analyses the constitutional and institutional mechanisms — Congressional appropriations authority, the War Powers Resolution, and senior military leadership — that constrain presidential overreach, and argues India should deepen ties with both Congress and the Pentagon rather than treat the White House as the sole interlocutor.
posts.author: Brigadier Anil Raman

posts.title: #13 DC Dossier 2025 Recap
posts.description: A year-end review of how the 119th Congress engaged with India-related legislation, hearings, and bilateral policy debates across 2025.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: #11 Partisan Divides and Strategic Expectations
posts.description: Key takeaways from the House hearing on the US–India strategic partnership, analysing how partisan lines shaped members’ priorities and the divergence between Democratic and Republican expectations of the relationship.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: #10 End of the Shutdown. Who Won and Lost
posts.description: Analysing the end of the longest government shutdown in United States history — which members and factions gained leverage, which lost it, and what the resolution signals for the 119th Congress’s governing capacity.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: #9 Trump’s Economic Policies Devastate His Base, Fuel Democratic Rout, and Imperil Midterms
posts.description: How the Trump administration’s economic policies — tariffs, spending cuts, and fiscal pressure — have translated into a Democratic sweep in off-cycle elections and what the trend implies for the 2026 midterms.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: #5 Understanding US Government Shutdown
posts.description: DCD Brief: the causes, key legislative flashpoints, and likely duration of the 2025 US government shutdown — and what it reveals about dysfunction in the 119th Congress.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: House lessons for Trump
posts.description: Kadiyala draws on the institutional history of the House of Representatives to argue that Trump's legislative strategy underestimates the chamber's capacity for obstruction — and that the thin Republican majority and fractious Freedom Caucus will prove a recurring constraint on the administration's domestic agenda heading into 2026.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala

posts.title: #4 Democracy First: The House’s Consensus on Pakistan Policy
posts.description: How does the 119th US House of Representatives view Pakistan? An analysis of bipartisan consensus — and its limits — on democracy conditionality, military aid, and human rights benchmarks in House engagement with Islamabad.
posts.author: Abhishek Kadiyala
